messages_body:
Hi Camila & Monica,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors from Redwood's API in our production tenant starting ~07:55 PST this morning. Latency is up (p99 ~6s, median ~1.2s) and error rate for text-generation calls spiked to ~5%. We've started routing traffic away from one application zone and still see the issue.

Grafana: https://grafana.zenithhealth.com/d/LLM/prod-errors?from=now-6h

Attached two screenshots showing the error rate and an example failed payload. Can you confirm whether Redwood made any infra changes or if there are known egress issues in us-west-2? We are blocking on a key release this morning and need an ETA.

Thanks,
Sara Li
Head of Platform Reliability
ZenithHealth

Attachment: error-screenshots.png

Sara — thanks for the prompt heads-up and sorry for the disruption.

We're opening an internal incident and looping Ops/SRE. Monica and I are on standby. Can you confirm the tenant id and whether you made any recent routing changes or peering updates from your side? Any sample request IDs or the HubSpot ticket would help.

I have looped in Neha (SRE) and Lauren (AE) to coordinate. We'll escalate to engineering if we see path-level issues.

— Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Camila's mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199

---- Original message ----
From: Sara Li <sara.li@zenithhealth.com>
Subject: Production: spike in generation latency + 5xx errors
Date: Fri, 28 Feb 2025 07:55:00 -0800

[attached: error-screenshots.png]

Camila / team — quick triage notes from SRE: we see the matching error-rate spike in our ingested telemetry. Early correlation: a subset of requests are timing out on egress to the model-serving subnet with TCP retransmits and increased DNS resolution timeouts.

I ran traceroutes from our edge to the ZenithHealth IP space and observed two distinct AS paths with differing latencies; one path shows an additional NAT hop and proxy inspection devices in the middle (likely a transparent proxy). I've attached the raw traceroute and a short tcpdump showing repeated SYNs + RSTs to one of the model hosts.

Preliminary artifacts: traceroute-zenith-02-28.txt, tcpdump-syn-samples.pcap (attached).

As next steps we recommend:
- Ask Zenith to confirm whether they rolled a VPC peering or egress NAT change at ~07:50 PST.
- Temporarily fail traffic to an alternate egress (us-west-2b) and disable proxy inspection for the suspect path.
- If Zenith confirms VPC/peering changes, request a peering route table dump and their DNS resolver config.

Looping in Vivek and Sean for operational approval for a temporary routing change / firewall rule exception.

— Neha Kapoor
SRE — Redwood Inference

Team — thanks Neha, and thanks for the artifacts.

I want to be explicit about risk and remediation: the symptoms and traces strongly suggest an egress path that includes a transparent proxy or DPI device on the customer's side (or their transit provider) that intermittently drops or delays SYN/FIN sequences to our model serving IPs. That explains the DNS TTL churn and asymmetric path latency.

Proposed immediate mitigation (low risk):
1) Programmatically fail requests from the impacted route to a known-good egress (configuration change in the routing layer) — this is software-only and reversible within minutes.
2) Provision a backup model-variant endpoint in us-west-2b and shift a portion of traffic (canary) while measuring errors.
3) Ask Zenith to temporarily disable proxy inspection for traffic to redwood-inference.* domains during the window.

I have a short playbook ready (playbook-emergency-egress.md) — recommend we get approval to run steps 1+2 immediately, then coordinate step 3 with Zenith's networking team. If we have exec-level pressure, we should also prepare a 1-page brief for their CTO.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

[Attached: playbook-emergency-egress.md]

Camila + Vivek — approve the immediate mitigations. Do it now.

I'll notify Sales leadership and tell them to hold the exec bridge. We need an ETA for customer-facing update in 30 minutes; assemble a short one-page for the customer and the execs.

— Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Success & Growth

On Fri, Feb 28, 2025 at 10:14 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — thanks Neha, and thanks for the artifacts.
> 
> I want to be explicit about risk and remediation: the symptoms and traces strongly suggest an egress path that includes a transparent proxy or DPI device...

Sara / Zenith team — update and next steps: 

We implemented an emergency egress failover at 09:42 PST to route impacted requests via an alternate NAT and us-west-2b egress. We also applied a temporary bypass for proxy inspection on the suspect prefix in coordination with our cloud provider. After the change:
- Error rate dropped from ~5% to ~0.4% within 10 minutes
- p99 latency improved from ~6s to ~1.1s
- No customer data was exposed; this change only affected routing for requests to model endpoints and is reversible.

Attachments: exec-brief-zenith-20250228.pdf (one-page incident summary), support-ticket-12345.txt (internal ticket).

Next steps:
1) We request Zenith's networking team confirm whether they rolled any peering or NAT changes at ~07:50 PST — route table dump and DNS resolver config would help.
2) We'll run a 4-hour monitoring window and then re-evaluate permanent routing or peering changes.
3) If Zenith cannot confirm, we'll keep the failover until a root-cause is identified and schedule a joint post-mortem.

Please confirm if you'd like us to schedule a 30-min exec sync (Sean + Vivek + Zenith CTO).

— Camila Reyes
